kill_fact: The floor has no mechanism, and four facts in the company's own filings -- none of which the dossier carries -- sit beneath it. (1) THE ISSUER DECLARES GOING-CONCERN DOUBT, AND THE BRIDGE CANNOT FUND THE COMPANY. The FY2025 Form 20-F, signed 19 March 2026, states: 'These conditions give rise to substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.' Critically, it also states that the $60 million bridge 'is ringfenced for the Kabanga Nickel Project', so corporate overheads, the Glencore PGM recycling investment and the IP segment 'will require near-term and alternative funding solutions', and that 'such solutions, which are required within the next 6 months, might include further equity offerings at the Lifezone Metals level.' Six months from that filing is about September 2026. This destroys the most favourable reading of the liquidity position: the $18.3 million still undrawn under the facility is NOT available to keep the parent alive, and the 20-F names further LZM-level equity as the expected route. The dossier never mentions the going-concern disclosure once, nor the ringfencing, across a document that purports to test what backstops the price. (2) SHAREHOLDERS HAVE NO ANTI-DILUTION PROTECTION. The same 20-F: 'the holders of Lifezone Ordinary Shares are not entitled to any preemptive rights or anti-dilution rights', and 'equity financing would dilute existing shareholders, who do not have pre-emptive or anti-dilution rights under our Articles of Association.' A declared going concern plus a named equity route plus no anti-dilution right is an unbounded downside, not a $2.00 floor. (3) THE COVENANT BREACH IS FILED, DATED, AND MISDATED BY THE DOSSIER. The 20-F sets a hard financial covenant: 'Lifezone is subject to financial covenants requiring it to maintain a current ratio of at least 1.1:1 on a consolidated basis while any amounts remain outstanding under the facility', plus a $5 million minimum cash balance at KNL. The Form 6-K furnished 29 June 2026 discloses that a waiver letter was executed on 7 MARCH 2026 by Lifezone, Kabanga Nickel Limited and Taurus, and that the company paid for it on 29 June 2026 with warrants over 500,000 ordinary shares at $6.25, five-year term. So the accommodation is not a 25 June third-party report that 'if accurate' would show fragility, and it is not an open question for the results call: it is a company-filed fact, dated nearly five months before the dossier places it, executed BEFORE the April placing and before management's 30 April 'concluding shortly' remark. The dossier also misses the 29 June 6-K entirely -- its timeline runs 25 June straight to 9 July. (4) THE FIRST BIG MONEY REPAYS THE LENDER, NOT THE EQUITY. The 20-F discloses a mandatory prepayment: KNL 'must apply any amounts received by it as repayment of the $60 million senior secured bridge loan facility on the date 10 business days after receipt' of proceeds from any transaction incurring financial indebtedness or any streaming, royalty, metals-prepay or forward transaction, 'provided that the total amount made available ... is at least $200 million' and funds Kabanga. The SocGen-led project financing that must accompany any build decision is precisely such a transaction. The security is on the shares in KNL itself, and a six-month maturity extension costs a further 1,500,000 warrants -- dilution priced into exactly the slip scenario being underwritten. Taken together: an issuer-declared going concern with a ~September 2026 parent-level funding need, no anti-dilution rights, a first-ranking lender that has already extracted equity once and holds a sweep over the refinancing, and a $2.00 'floor' derived by analogy to a peer trading multiple -- which is the identical criticism the dossier levels at the $2.60 it discards, and it fails the same test. A 2.8-to-1 ratio measured against an unbounded downside is not a defined-risk special situation, and this entry must not be carried as one.
corrections: MATERIAL. (1) OMITTED, load-bearing: the FY2025 Form 20-F carries an explicit substantial-doubt going-concern disclosure, states the bridge is ringfenced to Kabanga so parent-level funding is 'required within the next 6 months' (about September 2026) with further LZM-level equity named as the likely route, and records that holders have no preemptive or anti-dilution rights. Any floor written without these three facts is unsupported. This is the single largest gap in the dossier. (2) MATERIAL, factually wrong: the dossier asserts three times that 'the last filed balance sheet' is 31 December 2025. False. A 31 March 2026 balance sheet was furnished on 30 April 2026 (Form 6-K, Ex-99.1): cash $15.3 million at 31 March 2026 versus $20.1 million at 31 December 2025. Both sop_bear and valley_of_death derive from the superseded figures. (3) MATERIAL, wrong date and wrong evidential status: the Taurus waiver is not third-party analysis published 25 June 2026 that 'if accurate' would show accommodation, and it is not an open question for the 29 July call. The waiver letter was executed 7 March 2026 and consideration was paid 29 June 2026 as warrants over 500,000 ordinary shares at $6.25 (Form 6-K, 29 June 2026). The dossier's 'what nobody has asked -- this should be Wednesday's first question' is answered in a filing it did not read. (4) MATERIAL, omitted: the dossier's narrative arc runs 25 June to 9 July with nothing between, and calls the period one of silence. A Form 6-K was furnished 29 June 2026, and its content -- equity paid to the secured lender for covenant relief -- is worse for shareholders than silence. (5) OMITTED, load-bearing: the actual covenant is disclosed, not merely rumoured. Consolidated current ratio of at least 1.1:1 while any amount is outstanding, plus a $5 million minimum KNL cash balance of which at least $4 million must be in freely tradable currencies. Confirmed current liabilities were $59,080,398 at 31 December 2025. The dossier discusses 'covenant fragility' without ever citing or testing the covenant. (6) OMITTED, load-bearing: the mandatory-prepayment sweep. The first $200 million or more of project-finance or streaming money for Kabanga must repay the $60 million bridge within 10 business days. The financial close the thesis waits for pays the lender first. Note the sweep is drafted around debt-like and streaming transactions, so a pure equity injection into KNL may not itself trigger it -- but the project financing does. (7) MATERIAL: the transaction form is confirmed asset-level by primary source, not merely inferred. The Q1 2026 release describes 'a potential strategic investment into the Kabanga Nickel Project led by Standard Chartered Bank, with multiple offers received.' The 20-F describes Standard Chartered running a process to bring new investors into KNL. Both describe subsidiary-level participation, not a bid for LZM shares. The 40% weight on a $7.00 per-share event-win rests on a transaction form the filings do not support as the base case, so the $4.35 probability-weighted fair value is overstated at the top end. This does not by itself make the upside fake -- LZM retains 84% of KNL and a fairly priced injection accrues proportionally -- but it is not the takeout the $7.00 anchor implies. (8) MINOR, omitted: a THIRD undated gate. The 20-F states 'Finalization of the Joint Financial Model is a condition precedent for the Project FID', alongside the Framework Agreement amendment and the TANESCO power agreements the dossier does list. (9) MINOR, omitted: the six-month maturity extension is not free -- it requires issuing an additional 1,500,000 warrants to Taurus on substantially the same terms. The facility also carried a 2.25% arrangement fee, a 2.50% commitment fee on undrawn amounts, 9.25% interest, and 2.5 million warrants at $5.42 at inception. (10) CORRECTION IN THE BULL'S FAVOUR, for completeness: the dossier understates drawn liquidity mechanics. Of the $60 million facility, $25 million was drawn at 31 March 2026, a further $16.7 million was received 29 April 2026, leaving $18.3 million undrawn -- but per (1) this is ringfenced to Kabanga and does not relieve the parent-level going-concern need. (11) VERIFIED AS WRITTEN, so this is not a fake-asset kill: the catalyst is genuinely live and unfired -- no Form 6-K announcing a concluded sale or a build decision has been furnished through 27 July 2026; the 8 June 2026 response confirms 'the process to find a new strategic partner'; H1 2026 interim results are confirmed for 29 July 2026 at 10:00 a.m. ET; the bridge matures 31 July 2027 and is secured on the shares in KNL; live price $3.31, market value $297.6 million, 52-week range $3.02 to $6.40, 50-day $4.20, 200-day $4.49. The orebody is real and the process is real. The floor is not. evidence: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended 31 December 2025, Lifezone Metals Limited (CIK 0001958217), signed by CFO Ingo Hofmaier 19 March 2026. Going concern: 'As the senior secured bridge loan facility is ringfenced for the Kabanga Nickel Project, corporate overheads, the investment in the PGM Recycling Partnership with Glencore, other expenses linked to our IP segment and costs linked to business development activities, will require near-term and alternative funding solutions... Such solutions, which are required within the next 6 months, might include further equity offerings at the Lifezone Metals level. ... These conditions give rise to substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.' Shareholder protection: 'Under the A&R Articles of Association, the holders of Lifezone Ordinary Shares are not entitled to any preemptive rights or anti-dilution rights.' Covenant: 'Lifezone is subject to financial covenants requiring it to maintain a current ratio of at least 1.1:1 on a consolidated basis while any amounts remain outstanding under the facility. In addition, Kabanga Nickel Limited must maintain a minimum cash balance of $5 million in secured bank accounts, of which at least $4 million must be held in freely tradable currencies.' Confirmed current liabilities $59,080,398 (2024: $55,996,406). Facility: matures 31 July 2027, 9.25% interest, 2.25% arrangement fee, 2.50% commitment fee, 2.5 million warrants at $5.42 at inception; 'If the Borrower elects to extend, the Company will be required to issue an additional 1,500,000 warrants to Taurus Mining Finance'; 'secured by a security interest in the shares that Lifezone Limited... holds in the Borrower, and by security interests in other assets relating to the Kabanga Nickel Project'. Also: 'Finalization of the Joint Financial Model is a condition precedent for the Project FID'; 'we expect the Board of Directors to make the Financial Investment Decision for the Kabanga Nickel Project in 2026'. Subsequent events: 'As of December 31, 2025, KNL had $20 million outstanding under the senior secured bridge loan facility... On March 16, 2026, KNL received another $5 million from Taurus Mining Finance. This payment was an advance to the second drawdown of $21.7 million.'

Form 20-F (same filing), Item 10C Material Contracts, mandatory prepayment: 'KNL must apply any amounts received by it as repayment of the $60 million senior secured bridge loan facility on the date 10 business days after receipt by KNL or its group of any amounts advanced from the closing and initial utilisation of any one or a combination of (i) any transaction pursuant to which financial indebtedness is incurred; or (ii) any transaction involving the sale or delivery of any minerals... pursuant to a streaming transaction, royalty transaction, prepayment of metals agreement, metals forward sale or option... provided that the total amount made available for utilisations under these transactions (individually or in aggregate) is at least $200 million and the funding is being provided (all or in part) for capital expenditure or operating costs in connection with the Kabanga Nickel Project.'

Form 6-K, Lifezone Metals Limited, furnished 29 June 2026: 'As previously reported, on March 7, 2026, Lifezone Metals Limited (the "Company"), its wholly-owned subsidiary Kabanga Nickel Limited (the "Borrower") and Taurus Mining Finance Fund No. 2, L.P. executed a waiver letter with respect to the Borrower's $60 million senior secured bridge loan facility agreement. On June 29, 2026, pursuant to the waiver letter, the Company issued Taurus Mining Finance warrants to purchase 500,000 of the Company's ordinary shares, exercisable at an exercise price of $6.25 per share. The warrants will expire five years from the date of issuance.' This filing dates the covenant accommodation to 7 March 2026 and falsifies the dossier's 25 June 2026 third-party-report framing and its unbroken-silence timeline. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1958217/000121390026073112/ea0296311-6k_lifezone.htm

Form 6-K exhibit 99.1, 'Lifezone Metals Announces Q1 2026 Financial Results Summary', furnished 30 April 2026: 'Lifezone Metals reported a cash balance of $15.3 million as of March 31, 2026, compared to $20.1 million as of December 31, 2025'; '$25 million has been drawn from the senior secured bridge loan facility... The remaining $16.7 million under the second utilization was received on April 29, 2026, with a further $18.3 million under the facility remaining undrawn'; 'Negotiations progressed for a potential strategic investment into the Kabanga Nickel Project led by Standard Chartered Bank, with multiple offers received'; Framework Agreement amendment, staging concept and joint financial model still under negotiation; 220kV TANESCO line subject to 'ongoing negotiation of the Implementation Agreement and Power Supply Agreements'. The release contains no FID date of any kind -- the mid-2026 milestone was dropped silently, not reaffirmed. This establishes that a 31 March 2026 balance sheet exists, contrary to the dossier's repeated claim that 31 December 2025 is the last filed balance sheet. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1958217/000162828026028599/ex991nr8-26lzm2026q1interi.htm
